title: The Napoleonic Wars - OverSimplified (Part 1)
beats: NordVPN and patreon plug over a cold-open birth gag
Great conquerors have grand origins; Napoleon came from an obscure island, so how did he get here
Corsica sold to France by dialogue between Genoa and France; Napoleon born French and resentful
Father and son bicker in role-played voices, giving the family tension a face
Military school scene: Napoleon introduces himself to bullies; becomes lonely reader of conquerors
Promotion denied to the skilled in favor of a nobleman's son, which makes the old order concrete
Revolution framed as the answer to Napoleon's blocked ambition
Marriage to Josephine told as skits with recurring jokes
Revolutionary France and Austria as two characters chatting; Europe's monarchs react and war begins
Italian campaign: split the enemy in two and beat each half separately
Egypt flop then propaganda return; coup staged as protective cage dialogue
Second Coalition; narrator lists traits that made Napoleon great, one at a time ('one of them')
Alps crossing and Marengo, with the painting versus reality aside
Reforms as a stack of problem and fix pairs spoken as quick Q and A
Emperor, self-crowning; the ambition joke 'what comes after Emperor'
Third Coalition: second reason for his wins is speed via corps; then Napoleon shown doing it
Austerlitz trap told as fake baby-boy letter and enemy taking the bait, then fog reveals trick
Trafalgar shown with contrast: normal naval battle versus Nelson cutting the line
Fourth Coalition: Prussia goes alone, ignoring allies; ends with fast defeats at Jena, Friedland

metrics.ending: Cliffhanger-free stop after Friedland; part 2 implied

theory: OverSimplified teaches a sprawling timeline by giving every actor a recognisable voice and letting the same outcome recur, so the viewer induces the pattern (Napoleon beats coalitions) before it is named. Tension comes from the narrator's stated question (could the general also govern, 16:38) rather than from slowing down.
velocity: Scene builder: give each recurring entity a persistent avatar and voice so dialogue replaces exposition
Orchestrator: plant a promised list ('several reasons') and pay off one item per example, giving a built-in progress structure
Evals: check that a repeated pattern appears at least three times before the tutor names it
Voice: humor and pacing stay at constant wpm; vary beats rather than speed
quote: I don't know Pierre, what comes after Emperor?
